objective:
The old warehouse system exports stock corrections as a fixed-width file. Add a module `stockroom/fixedwidth.py` with a frozen dataclass `Adjustment(sku: str, delta: int, day: datetime.date, reason: str = '')` and the functions `parse_adjustments(text) -> list[Adjustment]`, `format_adjustment(adjustment) -> str`, `format_adjustments(adjustments) -> str` and `apply_adjustments(levels, adjustments) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]`. `Adjustment` is a plain record that does not check its fields (it holds any values it is given); the checks belong to `parse_adjustments` and `format_adjustment`. File and lines: if the text starts with U+FEFF, exactly one such character is removed first. The text is then split into lines at `
`, `
` and a lone `` (freely mixed; `
` is one line end); no other character ends a line (in particular not U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, form feed or vertical tab), and a line end after the last line does not create another line. Lines are numbered from 1 in this split, counting every line. A line that is empty or consists only of spaces (U+0020), whatever its length, is skipped. Every other line is one record; records come back in file order. Record layout, in 1-based columns counted in characters (code points) of the line (after the BOM removal): columns 1-10 SKU, 11-18 quantity, 19-26 date, 27-46 reason; a record is 46 characters. The checks run in this order and the first failure is reported. (1) A line longer than 46 characters is refused at column 47, even when the extra characters are spaces. A shorter line is padded with spaces to 46 characters (so trailing spaces may be missing). (2) SKU: columns 1-10 with trailing spaces removed must be 2 to 4 ASCII capital letters, `-`, and 3 to 5 ASCII digits `0-9`; anything else (a leading space, other Unicode digits, lower case) is refused at column 1. (3) Quantity: columns 11-17 must each be an ASCII digit (otherwise refused at the column of the first one that is not); column 18 is the last digit with the sign overpunched: `{` `A` `B` `C` `D` `E` `F` `G` `H` `I` mean a positive last digit 0 to 9, `}` `J` `K` `L` `M` `N` `O` `P` `Q` `R` mean a negative last digit 0 to 9, and a plain ASCII digit means a positive last digit; any other character is refused at column 18. The value is the eight digits as an integer with that sign (`0000012{` is 120, `0000012J` is -121, `00000123` is 123). A value of zero (with either sign) is refused at column 11. (4) Date: columns 19-26 are `YYYYMMDD`; each must be an ASCII digit (otherwise refused at the column of the first one that is not), and a date that does not exist, including year 0000, is refused at column 19. (5) Reason: columns 27-46 with trailing spaces (U+0020) removed; leading spaces and every other character are kept as they are (U+2028, U+00A0, U+FEFF, non-ASCII letters, quotes), except that a character of Unicode category `Cc` (control characters such as tab, U+0085, form feed) is refused at its own column. Every refusal is a `stockroom.errors.ParseError` whose message starts with `line L, column C:` (L the line number, C the column as above), for example `line 3, column 18: ...`. `format_adjustment` returns the canonical 46-character record without a line end: the SKU padded with spaces to 10 characters, the absolute quantity as 8 zero-padded digits whose last digit is always written with the overpunch character of its sign (`{`-`I` for positive values, `}`-`R` for negative ones, never a plain digit), the date as `YYYYMMDD` and the reason padded with spaces to 20 characters. It raises `ValueError` for anything it cannot write so that it reads back the same: a SKU that is not of the form above, a quantity of zero or of more than 99,999,999 in absolute value, a reason longer than 20 characters, ending with a space, or containing a `Cc` character. `format_adjustments` takes any iterable and returns every record followed by `
` (the empty text for no adjustments). `parse_adjustments(format_adjustments(rows)) == rows` for every list that can be written. `apply_adjustments(levels, adjustments)` takes `(sku, on_hand, reserved)` rows as `read_stock` returns them and any iterables, applies the adjustments in order of `day` (adjustments with the same day in the order given) by adding `delta` to `on_hand` (a SKU without a row starts at 0 on hand and 0 reserved), and raises `stockroom.errors.StockError` when an adjustment would leave `on_hand` below `reserved`. It returns the rows of every SKU, including untouched ones, sorted by SKU. Finally add `python -m stockroom reconcile --stock STOCK_CSV --file FIXED_FILE [--until YYYY-MM-DD]`, which reads the stock file, parses the fixed-width file (UTF-8), keeps only adjustments whose day is on or before `--until` when it is given, applies them and prints one line `SKU on_hand=N reserved=M available=K` (K = N - M) per SKU in that sorted order. Any error exits with code 1, `stockroom: error: ` followed by the error message on stderr, and empty stdout. Existing behaviour otherwise stays.
acceptance: The quantity field decodes overpunched signs: `0000012{` `A` `B` `E` `I` give 120, 121, 122, 125, 129; `}` `J` `N` `R` give -120, -121, -125, -129; plain last digits are positive (`00000123` is 123, `99999999` is 99,999,999); `9999999R` is -99,999,999 and `1234567}` is -12,345,670; a 10-character SKU, date 0001-01-01 and an empty reason are read

Lines may end in `\n`, `\r\n` or `\r`, mixed, with or without a final line end; one leading U+FEFF is ignored; lines without their trailing spaces are padded; empty and space-only lines of any length are skipped; the empty text, a lone BOM and only line ends give `[]`; U+2028, U+2029 and a U+FEFF inside a reason are data, and leading spaces of a reason are kept

Refusals report the exact line and column: a record of 47 characters (also with a trailing space) at column 47; bad SKUs (leading space, lower case, too few digits, Arabic-Indic digits, a second BOM) at column 1; a too-short line at column 11; non-digits in columns 11-17 (space, U+00A0, Arabic-Indic digit, `²` (U+00B2), `_`, `+`) at their own column; a bad sign character (`a`, `S`, space, `X`, `Z`, `²`) at 18; zero quantities at 11; non-digits in the date (`-`, full-width digit, `²`, a missing digit) at their column; impossible dates (2023-02-29, month 13, year 0000) at 19; control characters in the reason (tab, U+0085, form feed, vertical tab, U+0007) at their column; the line number counts skipped lines, `\r\n` and lone `\r` ends, and a U+0085 or form feed never ends a line

`format_adjustment` writes `MUG-001   0000012{20240309count               ` for 120 on 2024-03-09 with reason `count`, `0000012R` for -129, `0000000E` for 5, `0000000C` for 3, `ABCD-12345` `9999999R` `00010203` and a 20-character reason, keeps a leading space of the reason; `format_adjustments` ends every record with `\r\n`, gives `''` for none and accepts an iterator; `ValueError` for a zero quantity, 100,000,000 or -100,000,000, a lower-case SKU, a SKU with Arabic-Indic digits, a 21-character reason, a reason ending with a space, a tab or a newline in the reason

For 1,500 seeded random lists of up to six adjustments (SKUs of 2-4 letters and 3-5 digits, quantities from -99,999,999 to 99,999,999 without zero, every day from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31, reasons of up to 20 characters from letters, digits, spaces, punctuation, `é`, `日`, U+2028, U+00A0 and U+FEFF that do not end with a space): `parse_adjustments(format_adjustments(rows))` is `rows`, and so is parsing the same records with randomly removed trailing spaces, random `\n`/`\r\n`/`\r` line ends, extra blank or space-only lines, a missing final line end and an optional BOM; formatting the parsed result gives the canonical text again

For 1,500 seeded random valid files of one to five canonical records (joined by `\r\n` after zero to two leading empty lines) in which one character of one record is damaged, the error names that record's line number and the column where the damage is (column 1 for any damage in columns 1-10: a lower-case or Arabic-Indic or punctuation first character, or a `!` elsewhere in the SKU field; the damaged column itself for a non-digit (`x`, space, Arabic-Indic digit, U+00A0, `+`, `.`) in columns 11-26 and for a control character (tab, U+0000, U+0085, U+001F) in columns 27-46)

`apply_adjustments` adds deltas, creates rows for new SKUs, returns every SKU sorted (also for no adjustments and for iterators), applies a receipt dated earlier before a removal dated later whatever their positions, keeps the given order on the same day (the reverse order fails), and raises `StockError` when on hand would drop below reserved (13 of 14 with 2 reserved) or for a removal from an unknown SKU, while removing down to exactly the reserved quantity is fine

`python -m stockroom reconcile --stock S --file F` on a file with a BOM, mixed line ends (`\r\n`, a lone `\r`, `\n`), a short line, a blank line and a U+2028 in a reason prints `MUG-001 on_hand=6 reserved=2 available=4`, `NB-200 on_hand=40 reserved=4 available=36`, `PEN-100 on_hand=3 reserved=0 available=3`, `TEA-010 on_hand=55 reserved=5 available=50`; `--until` includes its own day (two cut-off examples); an empty file prints the unchanged levels; a bad record exits with code 1, empty stdout and stderr starting `stockroom: error: line 3, column 18:`, and a removal below the reserved stock exits with code 1, empty stdout and `stockroom: error:`
